title: Public prototype repository — software-to-physical provenance challenge

frozen_contract_probe.reason: The inspected source establishes software paths but does not establish that a particular calibrated physical sensor and actuator produced and executed a particular event. Promoting the code path to physical readiness would exceed the evidence.

gap.observed_fact: The public prototype contains gas-sensor read paths, a fixed analog threshold, remote event routing, and actuation logic, but the inspected repository does not establish hardware identity, calibration, health, physical binding, or historical runtime telemetry.
gap.why_current_contract_cannot_resolve_it: The frozen decision contract can represent a declared readiness state, but the inspected source does not establish the provenance required to promote the observed software path into a trusted physical-readiness fact.

non_claims: The presence of sensor and actuation code does not establish physical site readiness.
The repository does not establish that a specific physical sensor or actuator produced or executed a specific event.
The observed repository secret exposure does not prove the absence of every external hardware-bound provenance control.
This case does not count toward the B2 real-case minimum.
No automatic kernel rejection is claimed; the B2 evidence protocol withholds the unsupported physical-readiness assertion.
